newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO's Peru subsidiary sees output cut.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO's Peru subsidiary sees output cut.

text.p: ASARCO Inc said Tuesday that copper production at its subsidiary, Southern Peru Copper Corp, was expected to be reduced by about four million pounds for the first quarter as a result of rains and floods that partially curtailed operations last week.
Operations of Southern Peru Copper, in which it has a 54.1 percent stake, had returned to normal, ASARCO said.

The subsidiary had suffered from the heavy rains and floods that Asarco said damaged isolated sections of roadways, railroads and tailings system at the company's facilities and operations were partially curtailed as of March 3.
Southern Peru Copper, the largest mining company in Peru, operates the Toquepala and Cuajone mines and a smelter and refinery at Ilo, all located in the southern part of Peru.

The concentrators at the Cuajone and Toquepala mines and the solvent extraction/electrowinning plant at Toquepala returned to full capacity on March 6 while the smelter and refinery at Ilo returned to normal operations on March 10, it said.
Damaged roadways and railroad tracks have been temporarily repaired and permanent replacements will be made over the next several months, it said.
The subsidiary maintains property damage and business interruption insurance, it added.
Other owners of Southern Peru Copper are Marmon Corp (15 percent), Phelps Dodge Corp (13.8 percent) and common shareholders (17.0 percent).
